html:
Junkanoo is the street parade of the Bahamas, held in the early hours of Boxing Day and New Year's Day. It began among enslaved Africans, who were given a few days off at Christmas.

They danced in masks and costumes to goatskin drums, cowbells and horns. The name may come from an African leader called John Canoe. Similar festivals were held in Jamaica and the Carolinas.

After emancipation the parade survived despite bans. Today groups spend all year making huge costumes from cardboard and crepe paper, and compete on Bay Street in Nassau. Junkanoo music and dance are a core part of Bahamian identity, much as Carnival is in Trinidad.
sum: Junkanoo is the street parade of the Bahamas, held in the early hours of Boxing Day and New Year's Day. It began among enslaved Africans, who were given a few days off at Christmas.
